subject: Dedicated commit + burst add-on: surcharge structure and tradeoffs
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Liu <anna@scalegrid.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated commit + burst add-on: initial pricing options

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on ScaleGrid's throughput profile (3 peak services, mostly p95 < 400ms but a heavy tail during marketing events), I've sketched three burst/add-on structures you can choose from. Attached is a short packet with numbers and worked examples (RI_Dedicated_Burst_Options_v3.pdf). TL;DR options: 

1) Fixed Burst Slab (recommended for predictable events)
   - Pre-purchased burst credits in slabs (100k token-slabs / month)
   - Exhaustion -> enforced cooldown 10m + overflow billed at 0.08 USD/token-equivalent
   - Can carry-over up to 20% unused credits month-to-month

2) On-demand Surge (flexible, pay-as-you-go)
   - No pre-purchase; bursts billed at 0.11 USD/token-equivalent
   - Soft cap with automated fallback to a smaller model at 95th percentile if sustained beyond 30m

3) Hybrid (baseline reserved + capped surge buffer)
   - 12-month reserved commit for baseline (guaranteed throughput: 120M tokens/month across the GPU pool) at a 20% discount
   - Additional monthly surge cap: up to 2x baseline for up to 4 short events per month, billed at 0.06 USD/token-equivalent within cap, then 0.10 beyond

Key notes:
- Cooldown exceptions: we can offer an ops-approved exception path for one event/quarter with 48h notice. Otherwise cooldowns are automated to protect pool headroom.
- Throughput guarantees tie to the committed GPU pool sizing; if you choose the 12-month commit we’ll size the pool for the 95th percentile steady-state throughput and reserve burst headroom as per the slab/hybrid option.
- We can include a limited SLA credit for egregious sustained latency ( > 2x SLO for >60m) tied to committed baseline only.

Let me know which structure you prefer and I’ll pull together a formal term sheet. If it helps, we can also run a short load profile on a matched pool to validate sizing before you sign.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
attachments: RI_Dedicated_Burst_Options_v3.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)
From: Anna Liu <anna@scalegrid.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ScaleGrid Finance <finance@scalegrid.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit + burst add-on: initial pricing options

Diego —

Appreciate the clear options. A few immediate questions from my finance and infra leads: 

- The pay-as-you-go surge rate at 0.11 looks high relative to our forecasted token economics. Can Redwood do 0.08 as a cap for on-demand if we commit to a 12-month baseline?
- For the hybrid, what is the precise definition of an "event" that qualifies for the 4 short events / month cap? Our marketing spikes can be 2–6 hours.
- Cooldown automation: we need a manual escalation path for SEs to temporarily lift the cap during live incidents. What is the response SLA for that escalation?

Also finance would like to see an example invoice for a month with one large marketing spike — give us the delta between slab vs on-demand billing.

Can you loop in your pricing/legal folks — we may want the surge terms in the main MSA rather than an addendum.

Best,
Anna
CTO, ScaleGrid
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: ScaleGrid questions on surge pricing — need quick pricing counsel

Marissa / Connor —

Anna pushed back on surge rates and wants a manual escalation path. Can we draft a counter that protects our pool while giving a clear operational escalation and example invoice? Key asks: 1) lower on-demand cap to 0.08 if they take 12-month commit; 2) definition and duration for "event"; 3) SLA for manual exception.

Copy of Anna's questions below. I'm attaching the current packet. Please propose concrete language / numbers I can send back to them today.

Thanks,
Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: ScaleGrid questions on surge pricing — proposed counter

Diego / Connor —

Proposed counter (keeps risk bounded, gives ScaleGrid the commercial flexibility they asked for):

1) Commercial trade: 12-month committed baseline (minimum monthly spend equivalent to 120M tokens) with a 22% discount on baseline rates in exchange for a reduced on-demand surge cap of 0.08 USD/token-equivalent for any on-demand usage tied to that customer account. Baseline sizing and expected p50/p95 throughput to be validated in a 2-week pre-signing validation run.

2) Event definition and caps:
   - "Event" = a continuous period of elevated traffic where observed sustained token throughput exceeds baseline by >100% for at least 30 minutes.
   - Each "short event" may last up to 8 hours. The Hybrid package allows up to 3 short events per month (we can make it 4 for first three months as a ramp concession). Beyond cap: charges at 0.10 USD/token-equivalent.

3) Cooldown exceptions / escalation:
   - SEs may open an operations escalation via our Priority Ops channel. We guarantee a 2-hour acknowledgment and a 6-hour remediation window for escalations during business hours (24/7 if a P1 incident declared). One manual exception per quarter may be granted without additional surcharge if requested with >=48h notice; emergency exceptions considered case-by-case and billed at the hybrid beyond-cap rate.

4) SLA credit linkage:
   - We will include a limited latency SLA credit for committed baseline: if median token latency across the committed pool exceeds 2x the published SLO for >60 continuous minutes, customer receives a 10% monthly credit on the committed baseline portion for that month. No SLA credit for on-demand billed tokens.

5) Invoice example: I'll prepare a short spreadsheet showing a 6-hour marketing event where hybrid vs on-demand costs and include in the reply.

If Diego sends this to Anna I recommend we propose adding the surge terms into the main MSA (one paragraph + appendix) and include the 2-week validation run as a condition of signing.

-Marissa
Director, Commercials, Redwood Inference

Anna —

Thanks for the feedback. We ran this by Commercials and Operations and can offer the following, which matches Marissa's note below: 

Summary of agreed commercial approach (short):
- 12-month committed baseline sized at 120M tokens/month (22% discount on baseline rates).
- On-demand surge capped at 0.08 USD/token-equivalent for account-linked usage when baseline commit in place.
- Hybrid event rules: an "event" is >100% baseline load sustained 30+ mins; short events up to 8h; 3 short events/month (we'll allow 4/month for the first 3 months to ease your ramp). Beyond those thresholds, surge billing at 0.10 USD/token-equivalent.
- Manual escalation path: Priority Ops channel -> 2h ack / 6h remediation (business hours); 24/7 for declared P1s. One quarterly exception with >=48h notice at no surcharge.
- SLA credit: limited credit for committed baseline only (10% credit of committed baseline portion if median token latency > 2x SLO for >60m).

Next steps:
1) I'll attach a 1-page illustrative invoice and the revised redlines.
2) If this looks OK, legal can fold the surge terms into the MSA appendix.
3) We can schedule the 2-week validation run the week of Nov 29th — reply with preferred time windows.

Would you like me to route a DocuSign for the 12-month commitment + appendix after we get a quick legal thumbs-up? I can produce the DocuSign and the invoice example (links below).

Cheers,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
